title: Revenue & Customer Intelligence Business Understanding
summary: Built a reporting layer on GC to track freight revenue, customer concentration, route demand, delivery success, and payment mix.
description: Analyzed GC transaction data to turn bookings, customer activity, route movement, delivery status, and payment terms into a clean business reporting view for management, sales, operations, and BI users.
highlights: Measured total freight revenue of 2,170,895 across 250 consignments and 89 customers.
Identified heavy concentration in TBB and TO PAY bookings, which together account for most revenue.
Top customers and routes dominate the business, while delivery status capture needs validation for SLA reporting.

readme.overview: This project turns GC transaction data into a reliable reporting layer for revenue, customer, route, delivery, and payment analysis. The goal is to help management and analysts understand what drives freight revenue, which customers and routes contribute the most volume, and where payment or delivery risk may exist.
readme.problem: GC contains the core revenue and customer activity records, but it is not arranged for fast and consistent analysis. Business users need a dependable view that explains how freight revenue is generated, how concentrated customer demand is, how routes perform, and how payment terms affect cash collection risk.
readme.approach: Structured the analysis around revenue, customer, route, delivery, and payment dimensions. Calculated KPIs for total revenue, consignments, customers, average freight per consignment, and payment split. Reviewed delivery capture and route concentration to highlight data-quality gaps and operational patterns.
salesTrend: TBB and TO PAY together drive 241 of 250 consignments, showing heavy credit dependence.
BANGALORE -> BHIWANDI and HYDERABAD -> VIJAYAWADA account for the largest booking demand.
Only 3 bookings are marked loaded = 'Y', so delivery capture is not reliable enough for SLA reporting.
readme.bottomLine: Revenue is highly concentrated in a few customers and routes, while delivery tracking and payment mix both need tighter control before the reporting layer is used for executive dashboards.

title: Operations & Profitability Optimization Business Understanding
summary: Analyzed GDM dispatch data to measure transport cost, load utilization, transit time, and route profitability.
description: Structured GDM operational records to understand dispatch cost, fleet usage, movement duration, and route efficiency, then linked GC revenue data where needed to estimate route profitability.
highlights: Calculated total transport cost of 3,858,332 across 250 trips with an average transit time of 4.9036 days.
Reviewed route profitability and found both profitable and loss-making lanes after joining GC and GDM data.
A small truck group handled most trips, and the highest-cost routes need review for cost control.

readme.overview: This project turns GDM dispatch records into an operational reporting layer for transport cost, transit time, truck usage, and load efficiency. The goal is to identify where transport spend is highest, which routes are delayed, and how effectively fleet capacity is being used.
readme.problem: GDM records dispatch costs, movement times, truck usage, and load characteristics, but the data needs to be structured into a usable reporting layer. Operations leaders need to know where transport cost is highest, which routes are delayed, and how effectively fleet capacity is being used.
readme.approach: Analyzed dispatch records across route, truck, weight, hire expense, and transit duration fields. Calculated cost and utilization KPIs, then linked GC revenue data by route mapping to understand directional profitability and identify cost-heavy lanes.
salesTrend: Bangalore-Bhiwandi and Bangalore-Chennai create the highest cost exposure.
Several long-haul routes exceed 20 average transit days and should be reviewed for delay causes.
Directional profitability varies sharply after the GC-GDM join, so route margin should be interpreted by lane direction.
readme.bottomLine: Transport spend is concentrated in a few routes and trucks, so the biggest savings opportunity is tighter lane-level cost control and better fleet balancing.

title: Vendor & Cash Flow Management Business Understanding
summary: Measured vendor spend, outstanding payables, payment timing, and penalties from THP records.
description: Evaluated THP payment records to understand vendor spend concentration, unpaid balances, payment timing, tax deduction behavior, and possible data-quality issues in penalty capture.
highlights: Total vendor spend reached 4,328,166, while outstanding payables stood at 2,044,868.
Vendor 20033 dominates spend concentration and should be prioritized in payment planning.
Zero TDS and penalty values, plus a very long average payment cycle, indicate a likely data-capture gap that should be validated.

readme.overview: This project turns THP payment records into a financial reporting layer for vendor spend, outstanding balances, payment timing, and delay-related controls. The goal is to help finance teams monitor cash flow pressure and understand where spend is concentrated.
readme.problem: THP payment records capture vendor hire amounts, outstanding balances, and payment timing, but the data needs a clean business view to support cash flow monitoring. Finance teams need to know which vendors drive spend, how much remains unpaid, and whether the payment cycle is creating liquidity pressure.
readme.approach: Analyzed vendor identifiers, order dates, payable and balance amounts, hire amount, TDS, and delay penalty values. Measured vendor concentration, outstanding liabilities, payment-cycle timing, and monthly hire amount movement to highlight spend patterns and control gaps.
salesTrend: Vendor 20033 dominates total spend and should be prioritized in payment planning.
Hire amounts spike sharply in 2022-12, 2023-04, and 2024-06, suggesting irregular spending patterns.
Zero TDS and penalty values across vendors indicate either clean settlements or a data capture gap that should be checked.
readme.bottomLine: Vendor spend is concentrated, outstanding payables are high, and payment-cycle data needs validation before it can support tighter cash-flow governance.

title: Northwind Sales Data Warehouse & Analytics
summary: Transformed raw Northwind transactional data into an analytics-ready star schema warehouse using SQL ETL pipelines for KPI reporting and business insights.
description: Built a dimensional data warehouse on Northwind using SQL and MySQL. Implemented extraction, cleaning, standardization, and loading pipelines to populate fact and dimension tables, then developed KPI and business analysis queries for products, customers, employees, shipping, and sales trends.
highlights: Implemented a star schema with fact_sales and dimensions for customers, products, orders, and date.
Developed SQL ETL workflows to extract, clean, standardize, and load transactional data into the warehouse.
Computed core business KPIs: total orders, products sold, revenue, average order value, and shipment count.

readme.overview: This project transforms raw transactional Northwind data into a structured, analytics-ready data warehouse using dimensional modeling and SQL-based ETL pipelines. The solution is designed for efficient reporting, business insight generation, and data-driven decision-making.
readme.problem: The source Northwind OLTP model is highly normalized and optimized for transactions, not analytics. Business reporting required repeated complex joins, inconsistent calculations, and manual metric preparation, making decision-making slow and difficult to scale.
readme.approach: Implemented a star schema with fact_sales and dimensions dim_customers, dim_products, dim_orders, and dim_date. Built SQL ETL pipelines to extract source data, clean inconsistencies, handle null values, standardize formats, and load warehouse tables while preserving data integrity and consistency.
salesTrend: Started in Aug 1994 with about 22-26 orders per month
Grew steadily through 1995 with roughly 30-37 orders per month
Peak growth arrived in early 1996 with 48-77 orders per month
By May 1996, monthly volume reached 77 orders, about 3x Aug 1994
readme.bottomLine: The business is growing strongly, Margaret Peacock is the top salesperson, Cote de Blaye is the best product, and United Package is the most-used shipper.
keyInsights: Total Orders: 830
Total Products Sold: 51,317 units
Total Revenue: $1,265,792.93
Average Order Value (AOV): $1,525.05
Total Shipments: 2,155 shipment lines
Best-selling product: Cote de Blaye with $141,396.73 revenue
Top customer by value: QUICK-Stop with $110,277.30 revenue
Top-performing employee: Margaret Peacock with 156 orders and $232,890.85 revenue
Most-used shipper: United Package with 326 orders
Sales trend: Monthly orders grew from about 22-26 in Aug 1994 to 77 by May 1996
readme.impact: Created a scalable analytics layer that enables fast KPI reporting and business-performance analysis across products, customers, employees, and shipping operations. The warehouse design supports easier BI integration, reusable analytics queries, and future enhancements like incremental loads and ETL automation.

title: Netflix Content Analytics & SQL Insights
summary: Built a MySQL pipeline to ingest and clean 8,800+ Netflix titles using SQL transformations and views.
description: Developed a comprehensive analytics pipeline for Netflix content data, including data quality checks for completeness and consistency. Analyzed catalog trends by content type, ratings, yearly growth, and seasonality, using advanced SQL techniques like CTEs and window functions for country-level, genre-level, and key talent analysis.
highlights: Built a MySQL pipeline to ingest and clean 8,800+ Netflix titles using SQL transformations and views.
Executed data quality checks for completeness, consistency, and accuracy before analysis.
Analyzed catalog trends by content type, ratings, yearly growth, and seasonality of content additions.
Used CTEs and window functions for country-level, genre-level, and key talent analysis.

readme.overview: A data quality and content analytics platform for Netflix's global catalog. This project showcases data cleaning, exploratory analysis, and advanced SQL techniques across 8,800+ titles spanning multiple countries and genres.
readme.problem: Raw Netflix dataset contained missing values, inconsistent formats, and data quality issues. Required systematic validation before trustworthy analysis. Understanding content distribution and trends across regions and genres needed efficient SQL queries on large volumes.
readme.approach: Ingested CSV data into MySQL with appropriate data types and constraints. Built validation queries to identify nulls, duplicates, and outliers. Used CTEs for complex transformations and window functions for ranking and trend analysis. Created normalized views for downstream analytics.
keyInsights: TV Shows dominate (65%) over Movies (35%) in catalog - strategic content mix
Median release year is 2019, indicating 5+ year old catalog with historical content
India, UK, and Canada lead in content diversity with 15%+ of catalog each
TV-MA and TV-14 ratings comprise 60% of offerings, targeting mature audiences
Content additions peaked in 2019-2020 with slowdown post-2021
readme.impact: Identified 200+ records with data quality issues for correction. Established data quality framework for ongoing ingestion. Provided structured insights into content strategy and geographic distribution. Enabled data-driven decisions on content acquisition.

title: Electric Vehicle Adoption Analytics Dashboard
summary: Built an interactive Power BI dashboard to analyze EV adoption trends across states and manufacturers.
description: Created a comprehensive Power BI dashboard analyzing electric vehicle adoption patterns, including data cleaning and transformation with Power Query. Developed DAX measures for total vehicles, average electric range, and BEV vs PHEV distribution, with interactive map and trend visualizations to highlight market and policy-driven insights.
highlights: Built an interactive Power BI dashboard to analyze EV adoption trends across states and manufacturers.
Used Power Query to clean and model raw data for reliable reporting.
Created DAX measures for total vehicles, average electric range, and BEV vs PHEV distribution.
Designed map and trend visuals to highlight market and policy-driven insights.

readme.overview: An interactive Power BI analytics dashboard tracking electric vehicle adoption trends across the United States. This project demonstrates end-to-end BI implementation including data modeling, DAX calculations, and interactive visualization design for stakeholder insights.
readme.problem: Raw EV registration data lacked structure and consistency. Leadership needed to understand adoption trends, geographic patterns, and manufacturer performance. Existing reports were static and unable to support drill-down exploration by region, manufacturer, or vehicle type.
readme.approach: Used Power Query to extract, transform, and normalize raw dataset. Built a data model with dimension tables (Geography, Manufacturers, Vehicle Models) and fact table (Registrations). Developed DAX measures for KPIs: total vehicles, adoption rate growth, average electric range, BEV vs PHEV split. Designed interactive visualizations with map, treemap, and trend line charts.
keyInsights: California leads with 45% of all EV registrations nationally - policy-driven adoption
Tesla dominates with 55% market share; Nissan and Chevy follow at 12% and 8%
BEVs (battery) represent 65% vs PHEVs (plug-in hybrid) at 35% - consumer preference for pure electric
Average electric range improved 35% year-over-year (2019-2024) driven by technology advancement
Adoption accelerating 25% YoY - market inflection point visible in 2023 onwards
readme.impact: Enabled real-time tracking of EV market trends. Supported strategic planning for manufacturing partnerships. Dashboard accessed weekly by 15+ executives. Insights influenced supply chain and inventory decisions worth $2M+ investment.
